worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 30,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 14,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 30,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 14,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 14,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 14,250.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 14,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 4.7% x 14,250.00 = 669.75; line 13 = 669.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 14,250.00 = 669.75. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 669.75. Age 64 with household income under 45,000: a filer may qualify for the refundable Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit (up to 1,150, Form 2 line 16). It is a property tax relief credit, comes after line 10, and is not in the projection, so the expected tax is before it.
accepted_approximations: Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit: refundable, up to 1,150, for age 62 or older with household income under 45,000. Property tax relief outside the record.
